rule: The transcriptomics route is the notebook dev/distributable/plans/transcriptomics_workflow.rmd (793 lines) moved into KIT-093's kernels (R/func_trx_*.R) and renderers (R/func_trx_publication.R). This map is KIT-095's reading of each step's kernel with line evidence from those kernels and from the installed edgeR 4.10.1 (filterByExpr.default, filterByExpr.DGEList, cpm.DGEList, cpm.default, calcNormFactors.default as printed from the kit_093 library), RUVSeq 1.46.0, EDASeq 2.46.0 and ruv 0.9.7.1 (the kit_093 library, the versions KIT-093's environment.txt records). It is written before any declaration (ticket KIT-095 rev 1.1, planning gate). The units are determinations for KIT-095's declarations; a row with a flag is a question the user answers before the declarations. The design decisions the ticket already records (the user, 2026-11-06: RUVIII as a product-only export after DA with M as a parameter; the shared DA saving extended to the edgeR QL fit; parameterise, do not copy; the bindings hash is KIT-098's under protocol v1.8; no skip RUV mode; more than two groups refused) are applied, not reopened. The class TranscriptomicsAssayData (KIT-093) holds one count table in count_data and the design in design_matrix: no logCPM, W or newY is ever stored as a counts state; they are products.

units.row: each row's result depends on that row only (given the design and any declared global statistics)
units.complete_sample: each sample column's result depends on that column only (given any declared global statistics)
units.feature_group: depends only on the rows of one feature group (the grouping column is named)
units.whole_matrix: uses a statistic or model over all rows and samples; runs once on one projected object under the cap
units.store: not a data kernel: import, design, a store step, session export
units.products: writes plots or tables only; commits no state

kernel_observations: Determinism (KIT095-F13): the path uses no random numbers. ruv::ruv_cancorplot is svd plus cancor; RUVSeq::RUVs and ruv::RUVIII are svd with a fixed k; the edgeR fits (estimateDisp, glmQLFit, glmQLFTest) are deterministic. KIT-093 showed two consecutive runs identical() (kit-093/outcome.md, Determinism). The grid is sequential (lapply over the percentages, R/func_trx_ruv.R:28). Workers pin BLAS to one thread (R/utils_workflow_execution.R:1163); in-process runs are not pinned.

filterByExpr.DGEList (edgeR 4.10.1) passes lib.size = samples$lib.size * samples$norm.factors to filterByExpr.default; filterByExpr.default computes MinSampleSize from the group (tabulate, the large.n = 10 / min.prop = 0.7 adjustment), MedianLibSize = median(lib.size), CPM.Cutoff = min.count / MedianLibSize * 1e6 (min.count = 10), CPM = cpm(y, lib.size = lib.size), and keeps a row when rowSums(CPM >= CPM.Cutoff) >= MinSampleSize - 1e-14 and rowSums(y) >= min.total.count - 1e-14 (min.total.count = 15). Given lib.size every term is per row: the mask of a page equals that page's rows of the whole mask.

cpm.DGEList (edgeR 4.10.1) passes lib.size = samples$lib.size * samples$norm.factors to cpm.default; cpm.default with log = TRUE, prior.count = 2 computes each value in C (.cxx_calculate_cpm_log) from that count, the lib.size vector and the prior scaled by the lib.size vector: given the vector the value is per cell, so a page's logCPM equals that page's rows of the whole logCPM.

calcNormFactors (TMM, edgeR 4.10.1 calcNormFactors.default) needs every gene of every sample (the upper-quartile reference column and the trimmed log ratios): the TMM factors are a whole read, on the unfiltered counts for the filter and on the filtered counts for logCPM. The partitioned variants read the whole count matrix once for the factors (the pre-pass) and gain nothing in memory on the count matrix itself; they exist because the ticket asks for them and they are exact.

edgeR::DGEList refuses a matrix with no rows ('counts' must contain at least one value; audit KIT095-F05): a partitioned variant's template path returns the shell and never calls edgeR; the counts it records are read from the stored table shapes.

KIT-093's grid kernel (trxRuvGrid, R/func_trx_ruv.R:16-37) computes the preliminary QL ranking once (trxPrelimOrder, :41-47) and transposes logCPM inside each member (trxGridMember, :61). The per-member transpose is KIT-093's kernel and is not changed here (KIT095-F14 asks for the ranking once and no imputation; counts have no missing values, so KIT-085's prepareOmicsRuvCancorObject does not apply and no W1 is precomputed).

KIT-093's grid kernel computes its k cap itself (max_acceptable_k: 3 below 15 samples, else 4; R/func_trx_ruv.R:25). The ticket lists max_k with the default max_k_rule; the declaration follows the kernel (ticket: 'If KIT-093's kernels take different pre-pass arguments, the declarations follow the kernels, and the step map records the difference'): the rule is a fixed setting of trx_ruv_grid, its realised cap a record outcome, and manual_k above it is refused (trx_ruv_k_above_cap).

KIT-093's DE kernel (trxDaContrast, R/func_trx_da.R:46-66) fits and tests one contrast in one call. The ticket's one declaration per contrast on one saved fit takes its two halves: the fit (R/func_trx_da.R:50-61, DGEList, TMM, the realised design, the rank check, estimateDisp robust, glmQLFit robust) and the test (:62-63, glmQLFTest on trxContrastMatrix's column, topTags n = Inf by PValue). The calls, their order and their arguments are the kernel's; the halves are compared identical() to trxDaContrast and to the KIT-040 reference (fit_final, qlf, top_genes).
